name: 52-week high proximity level
note: George and Hwang's price level, not a price change: PH = close / the highest high of the trailing lb bars. Long while PH sits in the band [ph_lo, 1.00) AND the close is NOT a new lb-bar closing high AND no new high has been made in the last excl bars -- deliberately the opposite of a breakout, the trade is on price pinned just under the anchor and unable to get through it. Short when PH falls to ph_short. Entries are only considered every `every` bars, the monthly cadence of the original construction, and the hold is the time stop; early exit when PH leaves the band badly. TWO PARTS OF THE PUBLISHED RULE ARE NOT HERE and are not faked: the cross-sectional top/bottom 30% fleet rank needs every symbol at once, which a single-symbol ctx cannot see, and the six overlapping cohorts are a portfolio construction the shared one-position harness has no way to express.
source: Thomas J. George and Chuan-Yang Hwang, 'The 52-Week High and Momentum Investing', Journal of Finance 59(5), October 2004, 2145-2176, read at https://www.bauer.uh.edu/tgeorge/papers/gh4-paper.pdf -- stocks ranked on P_{i,t-1}/high_{i,t-1}, 30% cutoffs, 6-month hold. Grinblatt & Keloharju corroborate the price-level effect on Finnish account data.
